conclusion.justification: The report explicitly states that the claim is well supported by strong evidence from multiple randomized controlled trials, pooled analyses, and FDA approval, concluding that add-on CBD significantly reduces convulsive seizure frequency in children with Dravet syndrome.
conclusion.label: endorses

report:
This claim is well supported by strong evidence.

**Randomized controlled trials:** The pivotal study, published in the New England Journal of Medicine (Devinsky et al.), randomly assigned 120 children/young adults with Dravet syndrome and drug-resistant seizures to add-on cannabidiol (CBD) oral solution or placebo over a 14-week period. CBD reduced convulsive seizure frequency significantly more than placebo (median reduction ~39% vs ~13%) (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1611618). This finding was corroborated by a companion trial report (https://www.neurology.org/doi/10.1212/WNL.88.16_supplement.CT.001) and a second randomized dose-ranging trial published in JAMA Neurology testing two CBD doses against placebo, again showing significant seizure reduction (https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamaneurology/fullarticle/2762458).

**Pooled/long-term data:** A pooled analysis of two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials (GWPCARE1 Part B and GWPCARE2) confirmed that add-on CBD reduced Dravet-associated seizures, with results published in Epilepsia (https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/epi.17036). Long-term open-label extension data likewise showed sustained, clinically meaningful reductions in seizure frequency (https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1111/epi.14628).

**Regulatory confirmation:** Based on this trial evidence, the FDA approved Epidiolex (pharmaceutical CBD) specifically for Dravet syndrome seizures, and its Drug Trials Snapshot summarizes the supporting efficacy data (https://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-approvals-and-databases/drug-trials-snapshots-epidiolex).

**Conclusion:** Multiple independent, peer-reviewed randomized controlled trials, later reinforced by pooled analyses, long-term follow-up, and FDA approval, consistently demonstrate that add-on CBD significantly reduces convulsive seizure frequency in children with Dravet syndrome compared with placebo. The claim is accurate and reflects robust, replicated clinical evidence, though CBD is an adjunct (not a cure) and carries known side effects (e.g., somnolence, liver enzyme elevation, appetite changes).
